Description: The amount paid by the policyholder to the insurance company for coverage
Business Logic: Calculated based on risk factors and coverage amount; Must be paid to keep policy active

Description: The monetary value requested or paid for an insurance claim
Business Logic: Must not exceed policy coverage limits; Subject to deductibles

Description: The amount the policyholder must pay before insurance coverage begins
Business Logic: Higher deductibles result in lower premiums; Applied per claim or annually

Description: Unique identifier for each insurance policy
Business Logic: Must be unique across all policies; Used for all policy transactions

Description: Maximum amount the insurer will pay for a covered loss
Business Logic: Determined at policy inception; Cannot be exceeded regardless of actual loss

Description: The ratio of claims paid to premiums earned
Business Logic: Used to measure profitability and pricing adequacy; Lower is better for insurer

Description: Calculated score representing the likelihood of a claim
Business Logic: Based on actuarial models and historical data; Determines premium pricing

Description: Person or entity that owns the insurance policy
Business Logic: Must be legally eligible to hold insurance; Can differ from insured party

Description: Current state of a claim in the processing workflow
Business Logic: Follows defined workflow; Changes trigger notifications

Description: Sum of loss ratio and expense ratio
Business Logic: Industry benchmark for overall profitability; Below 100% indicates profit
